title: Serving Architecture & Request Paths
description: Study synchronous and asynchronous workflows, queues and backpressure, model routing and fallback, and streaming and cancellation. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Synchronous and asynchronous workflows
lessons.description: Design a submit, status and result API with an idempotent job identifier.
lessons.conceptOverview: Use synchronous responses for bounded interactive work and asynchronous jobs for long tasks with durable status. Provide request IDs and cancellation semantics so clients do not create duplicate jobs after timeouts.
lessons.whyItMatters: Long-running work benefits from durable asynchronous status.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Use synchronous responses for bounded interactive work and asynchronous jobs for long tasks with durable status. Provide request IDs and cancellation semantics so clients do not create duplicate jobs after timeouts.

lessons.title: Queues and backpressure
lessons.description: Calculate backlog growth over one minute and choose an overload response.
lessons.conceptOverview: Queues absorb bursts but do not create processing capacity. Bound queue size and waiting time, reject or defer excess work, and expose queue delay separately from execution time.
lessons.whyItMatters: Sustained arrival rates above capacity require admission control or more capacity.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Workers process 50 jobs per second while 80 arrive continuously. The backlog grows despite healthy workers.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Calculate backlog growth over one minute and choose an overload response. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Sustained arrival rates above capacity require admission control or more capacity.
commonMistakes: An unbounded queue fixes sustained overload.

lessons.title: Model routing and fallback
lessons.description: Specify fallback validation and an explicit unavailable response.
lessons.conceptOverview: Route by task capability, quality requirements and load. A fallback must preserve required behavior or explicitly degrade; silently switching to a weaker model can violate output or safety expectations.
lessons.whyItMatters: Fallbacks need the same contract or a declared degradation.

lessons.title: Streaming and cancellation
lessons.description: Trace cancellation through gateway, queue and worker and define partial-result handling.
lessons.conceptOverview: Streaming improves perceived responsiveness but does not necessarily reduce total compute. Cancellation must propagate to workers, and partially emitted output requires clear completion status.
lessons.whyItMatters: Cancellation should stop downstream work where supported.
